criteria.blocker: Three of the six named clauses fail at the release commit. The consent half of clause (c) is declared, migrated and never consulted by the routing decision; the relay's dead-letter queue is watched by nothing and then deleted by the retention sweep, so clause (d)'s durability is unobservable; and no cross-tenant notification delivery E2E exists, so clause (f) has no artifact at all. Separately, the catalog key chat.message.mention declares IN_APP+PUSH+EMAIL and has no production emit site.
criteria.clauses_failing: consent and suppression enforcement (the consent half); durable retry/DLQ behavior (the DLQ-observability half); cross-tenant notification delivery E2E. Clauses 'provider-response schemas', 'tenant-fair delivery/backpressure' and 'offline/revocation UI' were re-checked and now hold -- the remediation commit repaired them.
criteria.evidence:
FAILING CLAUSE (c) - consent is declared and never used. The tables exist in full: /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/db/schema/common/notifications-delivery.ts:295-296 (notification_consent_state / notification_consent_source enums), :304 notificationConsents, :337 notificationConsentEvents, with uniq_notification_consents_current, fk_notification_consents_actor and idx_notification_consent_events_subject. The file's own comment at :302 says 'legal basis. SMS and WhatsApp cannot legally ship without it.' The ONLY production consumers repo-wide are the GDPR export adapter (src/modules/gdpr/gdpr-export-adapters.ts:54-55) and a documentation ruling in organization/core/membership-artifacts.ts:1413-1420. `grep -n consent src/modules/notifications/notification-routing-computation.ts` -> exit 1: the routing decision has ZERO consent references and routes SMS/WhatsApp on preferences + policy + suppression rules alone. Consent is exportable and unenforced.

FAILING CLAUSE (d) - the relay DLQ is unwatched, then deleted. /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/scripts/alert-dead-outbox.mjs:62 reads `FROM outbox_events` -- the generic DOMAIN outbox, a different table from the notification relay's notification_outbox. `grep -rn 'notification_outbox|notificationOutbox' src/scripts/` returns only check-retention-coverage.mjs:127,230,240 (a retention policy entry) and a retention dead-man spec: no script queries notification_outbox for state='DEAD'. Meanwhile src/modules/cron/cron-notification-outbox-retention.service.ts:62 deletes `state IN ('PROCESSED', 'DEAD')` past the cutoff. And the alert that would cover it cannot fire: src/scripts/alert-dead-delivery.mjs:93 emits `destination: "CONFIGURE_ME -- wire exit-code 1 to your oncall system (PagerDuty, Slack webhook, etc.)"` and :97 `process.exit(fired ? 1 : 0)` -- zero rows exits 0 with no anti-vacuity floor, so silence is indistinguishable from health. Corroborating gate ground truth: `check:alert-ack` is exit 2, INCONCLUSIVE -- /tmp/beg-check_alert-ack.log reads 'PREREQUISITE MISSING: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is not set. Alert acknowledgement cannot be confirmed without a configured webhook destination.' Under the exit-code contract that is never a pass.

FAILING CLAUSE (f) - no cross-tenant notification delivery E2E. The territory's entire e2e tier is three auth-only files totalling 103 lines: src/modules/notifications/notifications.controller.e2e-spec.ts (39 lines, :34 `it.each(routes)("401 on %s %s without a token")`), src/modules/push/push.controller.e2e-spec.ts (42), src/modules/email/email.controller.e2e-spec.ts (22). `grep -rn 'cross-tenant|crossTenant|other org|foreign org'` across all three -> exit 1. What does exist is DB-level, not E2E: src/modules/push/push-subscription-ownership.db.spec.ts:260 and src/modules/email/unsubscribe-scope.db.spec.ts (11 tests) close the storage layer but never drive HTTP with two seeded orgs.

NAMED FACT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY - chat.message.mention has NO production emit site. Every reference at head (`grep -rn 'chat.message.mention' src --include='*.ts' --include='*.mjs'`, excluding .claude/worktrees which are a detached branch): notification-events-chat.catalog.ts:12 -- the catalog declaration itself, `notificationEvent("chat.message.mention", "chat", "CHAT", "You were mentioned", { defaultPriority: "HIGH", defaultChannels: IN_APP_PUSH_EMAIL, dedupeWindowSeconds: 0 })` -- plus three spec fixtures (notification-fanout-isolation.spec.ts:46, inbox-section-keys.spec.ts:8, unsubscribe-scope.db.spec.ts:94). Nothing dispatches it. The live path is src/modules/chat/chat-message-fanout.service.ts:141 -> chat-notifications.service.ts:109 publishMentionNotification -> :151 `this.ably.publishToUser(orgId, userId, "notification:mention", payload)` -- Ably realtime only; no NotificationDispatchService call, no durable notification row, no email, no web-push. Chat DOES use NotificationDispatchService, but only for chat.huddle.invite and chat.reply.reminder. Consequence: a mentioned user who is offline receives nothing durable, despite the catalog promising in-app + push + email at HIGH priority. The gate that would catch this, `verify:chat-mentions`, is red for a prerequisite rather than a finding: /tmp/beg-verify_chat-mentions.log is 327 bytes of the AUTH_SIGNING_KEYS guard, exiting 1 before any assertion (it also needs a booted API on :1500 and ABLY_API_KEY) -- so it is neither evidence of the defect nor evidence against it, and it exits 1 where the contract wants 2.

REGRESSION FOUND IN THIS TERRITORY (not in any prior report). `check:cycles` is RED at head with exactly ONE circular dependency repo-wide, and it is in the notification delivery path: /tmp/beg-check_cycles.log reads 'Found 1 circular dependency! 1) modules/notifications/notification-delivery-worker.service.ts > modules/notifications/notification-delivery-preflight.ts'. Verified at source: src/modules/notifications/notification-delivery-worker.service.ts:51 `import { resolveDeliveryPreflight } from "./notification-delivery-preflight"` and src/modules/notifications/notification-delivery-preflight.ts:9 `import type { QueueRunResult } from "./notification-delivery-worker.service"`. Shared CLAUDE.md section 9 requires the import graph to stay acyclic ('both repos are at zero') and prescribes moving the shared type to a neutral module -- notification-delivery-types.ts already sits beside it and is imported at :8, so that is where QueueRunResult belongs. `git log -- notification-delivery-preflight.ts` shows the file was introduced by 74125165c 'fix(gates): close eight red gates by fixing the code', i.e. the gate-closing commit opened this one.
